newsitem.title: GERMANY: Augsburg, Crossair protest at St Tropez flight ban.
newsitem.headline: Augsburg, Crossair protest at St Tropez flight ban.

text.p: German regional carrier Augsburg Airways said it has had to cancel its flights to St Tropez after French authorities banned foreign airlines at short notice.
The airline was forced to drop its inaugural flight in Team Lufthansa colours from Munich on April 6 at just two days' notice, a statement said.
The French transport ministry has banned aircraft weighing more than 5.7 tonnes or with more than 10 seats from landing with immediate effect, it added.
Augsburg Airways planned to operate the weekly route as a code-share flight under its franchise agreement with Deutsche Lufthansa AG with a 50-seat Dash-8 aircraft.
Augsburg Airways managing director Olaf Dlugi said: "We are outraged at the decision and especially that we were informed at such short notice.
"During our discussions about launching the service nothing was ever said about the transport ministry having such plans," he added.
It appeared the French authorities were trying to prevent foreign competition to Nice airport just days after full liberalisation of the European air travel market on April 1, he said.
There was no technical reason to ban flights since Swiss airline Crossair had flown without problems for two years to the airport, which had sight-only landing facilities.
Swiss airline Crossair flies twice-weekly from Geneva to St Tropez with a 34-seat Saab 340.

Augsburg Airways, Lufthansa, Crossair and the European Regional Airlines Association (ERA) have protested to the authorities over the decision and have demanded a written explanation, the statement added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
